newsitem.title: USA: Primark sees additional restructuring cost.
newsitem.headline: Primark sees additional restructuring cost.

text.p: Primark Corp said Wednesday measures taken at Groupe DAFSA to lower operating expenses and to integrate certain marketing and production operations with other Primark units will result in a restructuring cost of about $6.5 million.

Primark had reserved $1.5 million for restructuring costs at the time of DAFSA's acquisition in June of 1996, so the additional charge expected for the second quarter is $5.0 million. The plan being implemented should enable DAFSA to reach positive cash flow during 1997.
"We are well on the way to resolving the operating problems encountered by two of Primark's subsidiaries," said chief executive Joseph E. Kasputys.

"It is important to understand that the businesses constituting 99 percent of our information services segment are healthy and performing well. The exception is DAFSA, which was acquired last June for its financial databases. Largely due to poor results in unrelated lines of business, we are eliminating certain operations and making major cost cuts."

He said "TIMCO's second quarter performance will improve due to renegotiation of the contract for the major overhaul of five DC-10 aircraft. Otherwise, TIMCO's business prospects are excellent with only the industry-wide labor shortage holding back the potential for near-term margin growth."
Primark reported net income from continuing operations for the first quarter 1997 of $4.1 million, or $0.15 per share, compared with $6.1 million, or $0.23 per share, for the first quarter last year.
The losses at Groupe DAFSA reduced profitability at TIMCO, the company's aircraft maintenance subsidiary, and unfavorable foreign currency movements, the company said.

Results were helped by a $2.0 million gain on the sale of the company's interest in The Weather Network, a joint venture weather business located in the UK. Offsetting this gain was a $1.8 million restructuring charge at Disclosure Inc, where investments in new information technology and the ongoing shift from paper-based documents to desktop electronic delivery have enabled productivity improvements. This restructuring charge is largely related to the elimination of more than one hundred positions at Disclosure.
